scope: Federal parameters for Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, SNAP, SSI, the ACA marketplace, the poverty guidelines and the UI financing basics in effect during 2026, plus Pub. L. 119-21 changes and dates. Per-place: Medicaid expansion, FMAP where verified, nutrition program type, SSI availability. Per-state FY2026 FMAPs, non-expansion parent limits, SNAP error rates and territory Medicaid caps are UNKNOWN.

piaFormula.value: 90% of AIME up to the first bend point, plus 32% of AIME between the bend points, plus 15% of AIME above the second bend point
piaFormula.note: Formula percentages are statutory (42 U.S.C. 415(a)); bend points apply to workers first eligible in 2026.

1942-and-earlier.question: SSA retirement-age table rows for birth years before 1943 (not needed for a 2026 world but not verified here)

delayedRetirementCreditPctPerYear.note: For birth years 1943 and later; accrues to age 70.

spouseBenefitMaxPctOfPia.note: Delayed credits do not raise the spouse benefit; early claiming reduces it (spouse reduction schedule UNKNOWN here).

familyMaximum.question: Family maximum formula bend points for 2026

diDepletion.question: 2025 Trustees DI fund depletion year (believed not depleted within 75 years; unverified)

trustees2026.note: The 2026 report came out 06/09/2026 and supersedes 2025 for game calibration.

longRangeDeficitPctPayroll.note: up from 3.82; figure from secondary summaries (BPC/JPMorgan), secondary

effect.value: Repeals the Windfall Elimination Provision and the Government Pension Offset

effectiveFor.value: Monthly benefits payable after December 2023 (retroactive to January 2024)

retroPaymentsBegan.note: snippet-derived from secondary pages in the same result set

appliesIn.question: Source confirming Social Security covers all 50 states, D.C., PR, GU, VI, AS and MP (expected yes; no snippet captured)

partAPremiumBuyInFull2026Monthly.note: for people with fewer than 30 quarters

irmaa2026.question: 2026 IRMAA income brackets and Part B/D surcharges

appliesIn.question: Source confirming Medicare covers all 50 states, D.C. and the five territories (expected yes; no snippet captured)

expansionFmapPct.note: statutory 90% for newly eligible adults since 2020

arpaExpansionIncentiveEnds.note: P.L. 119-21 ended the ARPA 5-point incentive for newly expanding states

fmapFloorPct.note: 10 states at the 50% floor in FY2026; which ones is UNKNOWN here

stateFmapTable.question: Per-state FY2026 FMAP from 89 FR 94742 table; the Federal Register, govinfo and MACPAC pages were blocked, so only MS, DC and territory rates are recorded.

nonExpansionParentLimits.question: KFF 'Medicaid Income Eligibility Limits for Parents' 2026 by state; only tertiary sites seen (TX ~17-18% FPL, AL ~18% FPL), not recorded as values

whoMustComply.value: Expansion adults (and 1115-waiver adults with comparable coverage) aged 19-64

hoursPerMonth.note: work, community service, work program, or education, or a combination

statutoryStart.note: CMS rule describes the compliance date as 01/01/2027; statute permits good-faith exemptions to 12/31/2028 (that extension date is UNVERIFIED here)

value: parents/caregivers of a child 13 or younger or a disabled person
people in a SNAP household meeting SNAP work rules
exempt.note: Other exemptions (veterans with disability ratings, inmates recently released, people in treatment, under-21 former foster youth) UNKNOWN here

sixMonthRedeterminations.value: Expansion adults, for renewals starting after 12/31/2026

retroactiveCoverage.note: month limits from a secondary snippet; date from CRS snippet

value.expansionStatesHoldHarmlessThreshold: 6.0% stepping down 0.5 point a year to 3.5%

providerTaxes.note: Start date conflict: summaries say both 'FY2028' and 'beginning 10/01/2028'; UNKNOWN which (research question: first fiscal year of the 5.5% threshold)

emergencyMedicaidFmapLimit.value: Emergency Medicaid for noncitizens matched at regular FMAP, not the 90% expansion rate, from 10/01/2026

immigrantEligibility.value: Federal Medicaid limited to citizens/nationals, LPRs, Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA migrants from 10/01/2026

ruralHealthTransformation.note: CMS RHT program page in the same result set

stateTriggerLaws.value: Utah changed its expansion end-date trigger in 2026; Idaho and Oklahoma repeal efforts did not pass

earnedIncomeDeductionPct.note: snippet from CBPP guide in the same result set

benefitRule.value: Benefit = maximum allotment minus 30% of net income
benefitRule.note: The 30% expected contribution is statutory; captured only indirectly

otherRegionsFy2026.question: FY2026 maximum allotments for AK, HI, GU, VI by household size

value.fy2028Basis: lower of FY2025 or FY2026 error rate
value.delay: states with error rate x 1.5 >= 20% (>=13.33%) delayed: FY2025 rate -> 10/01/2028; FY2026 rate -> 10/01/2029

stateBenefitCostShare.note: 15% top tier inferred from 'range 0 to 15%'; confirm against statute

value.waivers: only areas with unemployment above 10% (special rules for AK, HI)
value.effective: on enactment 07/04/2025; USDA implementation guidance followed

abawd.note: exact implementation date per USDA memo UNKNOWN

snapEd.value: Federal SNAP-Ed funding ends after FY2025

noncitizens.value: Narrowed eligible lawfully present noncitizen categories

thriftyFoodPlan.value: Future re-evaluations must be cost neutral (effective on enactment)

pendingFarmBill2026.value: Senate Agriculture passed a farm bill 09/16/2026 that would delay the benefit cost share one year to 10/01/2028; not law as of 09/28/2026; House bill has no such delay

2026.note: eachAdditional 5680 is derived as (33000-15960)/3; one snippet said 6530, which does not fit the published family-of-4 figure. Published 01/15/2026 (FR 2026-00755); October 2025 CPI missing due to shutdown.

povertyGuidelines.note: Medicaid and the ACA use the prior-year guideline for coverage years in part; the game should key each program to its own guideline year.

enhancedCreditsStatus.value: Expired 12/31/2025; House passed a 3-year extension 01/08/2026 (230-196); Senate did not pass it; not extended as of late August 2026

applicablePercentage2026.note: endpoints from snippets quoting Rev. Proc. 2025-25; 9.96 also the 2026 employer affordability percentage

benchmarkPremium40yoMonthly.question: KFF average benchmark premium for a 40-year-old, 2026 (a $497 figure appeared only on a tertiary site)

availableIn.value: 50 states, D.C., and the Northern Mariana Islands only

value.holding: 8-1: the Constitution does not require Congress to extend SSI to Puerto Rico residents
2020 district ruling for Guam vacated as moot by the Ninth Circuit in April 2022 after the plaintiff died

unemploymentInsurance.note: Lane A owns spec 1; basics only.

borrowing.value: States may take Title XII advances from the federal Unemployment Trust Fund; after two consecutive January 1 balances unpaid by November 10, employers lose 0.3 point or more of the FUTA credit

creditReductionStates2025.note: 0.6-point reduction reported for CA, CT, NY and VI in one snippet; final 2025 list per FR 2026-00342 not opened
